newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re to post strong profit, but outlook muted.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re to post strong profit, but outlook muted.

text.p: German reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG is poised to post a sharp rise in its 1995-1996 profits next week, but analysts say its future earnings outlook is more muted.

Munich Re, the world's largest reinsurer and a newcomer to Germany's blue-chip DAX share index, has already reported a surprising surge to 140 marks in its earnings per share in the period, prompting it to up its dividend to 16 marks from 13.50.
"That kind of dividend hike -- 2.50 marks -- is on a level we had never seen before and is a clear sign of how well earnings went last year," said BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein.

Munich Re will elaborate on its results at a news conference on Monday and is expected to reveal an exceptionally good underwriting result, leading to net profit well above the previous year's 325 million marks ($215.4 million).

Given that EPS data has already been released, Hein and other analysts are generally not issuing forecasts for Munich Re's 1995-1996 net profit, which is not considered the most important indication of its profit situation.

"They have already reported such a strong profit improvement that I cannot expect much more market reaction, at least on the upside," said Lars Niggeling, analyst at Trinkaus Capital Management in Duesseldorf.

Munich Re's shares have surged since its registered stock was introduced to the DAX index in September, the result of the group's long campaign for recognition as one of Germany's most heavily capitalised companies.

A rally in the run-up and aftermath of the DAX inclusion left Munich Re's registered stock trading Thursday at 3,715 marks, a jump of more than a third from the year low of 2,700 marks hit at the end of June.

However analysts said that longer term prospects for the group were more muted, especially given the rising price pressures in the primary insurance market which are already making themselves felt in reinsurance.

Munich Re is expected to experience additional pressure on earnings in the current business year due to its $3.3 billion takeover of American Re in a mega deal agreed this year and to be completed shortly.

And despite the earnings upsurge in 1995/1996, Munich Re has already said its premium income, a measure of its business volume, rose by only 100 million marks to around 29.1 billion marks in the period.

"The times for significant earnings increases in reinsurance are over. We cannot expect claims to improve at the same rate as they have in the last few years and prices are also not going to rise as they have," BHF's Hein said.
